newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar boosts German shares to record close.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar boosts German shares to record close.

text.p: European stock markets extended gains on Monday afternoon, with the strong U.S. dollar boosting German shares more than two percent to a record high bourse close.
The dollar lingered near a six-year peak against the mark as the German unit dropped to the lowest level against sterling since October 1990 and to a 23-month low versus the yen.
Expectations of more British rate increases after the Bank of England raised the base rate a quarter point last week kept sterling buoyed above 3.02 marks.
The dollar also gained against the mark after Austrian National Bank General Director Adolf Wala said he expected the dollar to reach 1.80 marks, compared with current levels just over 1.79.
"The current development of the dollar/mark is actually an adjustment to real consumer spending parity," Wala said. "I expect (dollar/mark) to find its level at 1.80."
Traders said continued dollar strength would help make more European exports cheaper abroad and lift exporters' profits.

"What we've seen (in German stocks) so far is perfectly justified with the dollar at this level," a Frankfurt dealer said when Germany's IBIS DAX index hurdled 4,100 points for the first time in pre-bourse, electronic trade.
The bourse-traded 30-share DAX index closed at a record high 4,124.19 points, just off its all-time intraday high of 4,127.97.
Leading German shares included dollar-sensitive drug, engineering and car stocks. Drugs group Schering AG ended up 3.20 marks at 198.50, off its year high of 199.40 set earlier.
Engineering firm Siemens AG rose 2.05 to 114.65, also just off its year high of 115.45 hit earlier in the session.
Swiss shares held most of their opening gains to stand more than a percentage point higher, also with the dollar's help.
Winterthur Schweizerische Versicherungs-Gesellschaft added to its early gains, jumping 57 Swiss francs to 1,475 by 1410 GMT on merger or takeover speculation.
London's FTSE 100 index advanced to session highs on merger speculation and Wall Street's rise at the open.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up on expectations of positive second-quarter earnings reports.
In London, "everyone is talking about mergers," a dealer said. "Sterling worries and rate rises have been pushed into the background."
Sterling's jump was seen capping FTSE gains earlier.
"The consumer sector will continue to lead the rise despite the strength of sterling, especially with hints of merger activity in the background," another dealer said.
Commercial Union Plc also jumped about 2.5 percent in the afternoon, extending gains from Friday on speculation ABN AMRO Holding NV may buy the firm.
WH Smith rose on weekend press reports the UK retailer may be a bid target after its shares slid about 30 percent in the past two months.
Commercial Union was up 23-1/2 pence at 704 pence, and WH Smith was up 8-1/2 at 351 pence at 1425 GMT.

Chemicals giant Imperial Chemical Industries Plc was also among the winners, reaching a year high after it said it agreed to sell its polyester polymer, titanium dioxide and polyester film businesses to U.S. firm DuPont Co for $3 billion.
In mid-afternoon, ICI was at 887 pence, near its year high of 890.
Paris markets were closed for the Bastille Day holiday.
CURRENCIES AT 1425 GMT
The dollar was little changed at 114.00 yen and 1.7917 marks versus 113.85 and 1.7705 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1425 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 42.3 points at 4,841.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 83.22 points at 4,124.19.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 12.50 points at 2,941.59 on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold 1500 fix was at $321.70, up from $320.05 an ounce at Friday's close. Silver was at $4.33.
